title: The Association of Hospital Characteristics With Medicaid Managed Care Hospital Prices

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《The Association of Hospital Characteristics With Medicaid Managed Care Hospital Prices》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · hesr70178-sec-0006-p3】The objective of this study is to examine how negotiated Medicaid managed care hospital prices for routine procedures in hospital outpatient or ED settings differ by the following hospital characteristics: children's hospital; critical access hospital (CAH) [23]; rurality; system affiliation; teaching designation; for‐profit, religious affiliation, or government ownership; and size.

【Introduction · hesr70178-sec-0006-p1】The price of care for a given procedure varies substantially across hospitals [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. Market dynamics may play a role in this price variation. Over the last 25 years, the consolidation of hospitals has reduced competition [6], and several studies show that hospital prices can increase following mergers [7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13]. Furthermore, some hospitals, such as teaching hospitals, often provide unique services, advanced care, or brand recognition that are not easily substituted; as such, they may wield substantial negotiating power during contract discussions with insurers [14]. It follows that certain hospital characteristics, like teaching status and ownership type, may be associated with market power [6].

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《The Association of Hospital Characteristics With Medicaid Managed Care Hospital Prices》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Study setting and design · abstract-2-1】We conducted a cross-sectional study of facility claims data from Elevance Health-affiliated Medicaid plans from 22 states plus D.C. We estimated Poisson regression models where the outcome was facility allowed cost ("price") for procedures of interest, and the exposures were hospital characteristics, including children's hospital, critical access hospital (CAH), rurality, system affiliation, teaching designation, for-profit, religious affiliation, government ownership, and hospital size. We report incidence rate ratios (IRRs) from the regression estimates.

【Data Sources and Claim Identification · hesr70178-sec-0008-p2】For children, we examined the following procedures: tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy, tympanostomy, splinting, and ED evaluation and management (E/M) Levels 2–5. For adults, we examined the following procedures: knee arthroscopy, colonoscopy, obstetric ultrasound, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain, and ED E/M Levels 2–5. For each procedure, we only included claims in either the hospital outpatient department (HOPD) setting or the ED setting. eTable 1 lists the Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes used for each procedure as well as the required setting. We selected common, routine procedures for the study. Focusing on routine outpatient and ED procedures reduces the likelihood that observed differences in prices are due to patient or procedure complexity; routine procedures are also common in the claims data, which allows for a greater sample size for the analysis. We also included multiple procedures, rather than focusing on a single procedure, because higher prices at a given hospital type may be heterogeneous based on procedure. Inpatient claims were not included due to the complexities in billing for inpatient services that make direct comparisons more difficult, especially for facility claims. Lastly, we used all claims from any hospital; if a hospital only had claims for some of the procedures of interest, it was still included in the analysis. For example, if a hospital did not have any tympanostomy claims during the study period but claims for all other procedures, then that hospital would be excluded from the tympanostomy analysis but included in other procedures' analyses.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《The Association of Hospital Characteristics With Medicaid Managed Care Hospital Prices》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusions · hesr70178-sec-0017-p1】This analysis found that children's hospitals were associated with substantially higher Medicaid managed care prices than other acute hospitals for several common outpatient and ED pediatric procedures. CAHs also tended to have higher prices for both children and adults. Results were mixed for the other hospital characteristics, depending on the procedure. More research is needed to understand what is driving the observed differences in hospital prices by various hospital characteristics.

【Principal findings · abstract-4-1】The largest price differences were at children's hospitals and CAHs. For all child procedures, prices were higher at children's hospitals relative to other acute care hospitals: the largest estimate was for ED E/M Level 2 (IRR = 2.51; 95% CI, 2.14-2.95). Children's hospital estimates represented 93%-151% higher prices for ED procedures and 23%-48% higher prices for outpatient procedures. CAHs had higher prices for almost all procedures: for children the largest estimate was for tympanostomy (IRR = 1.78; 95% CI, 1.45-2.18), representing 78% higher prices, and for adults the largest estimate was for MRI (IRR = 2.43; 95% CI, 2.13-2.76), representing 143% higher prices. Results were mixed for other hospital characteristics.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《The Association of Hospital Characteristics With Medicaid Managed Care Hospital Prices》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【FIGURE 1 · hesr70178-fig-0001】FIGURE 1 Percentage of select procedures occurring in different hospital types. CAH, critical access hospital; ED, emergency department. Percentages sum to more than 100% for each setting (i.e., ED or outpatient) because hospitals were characterized as more than one type. For the adult population, claims from children's hospitals were excluded.

【FIGURE 2 · hesr70178-fig-0002】FIGURE 2 Coefficient plots for child population. CAH, critical access hospital; ED, emergency department; E/M, evaluation & management. The outcome is allowed cost for each procedure (capped at the 99th percentile). Regressions include all explanatory variables in the figure as well as a hospital wage index variable, state fixed effects, and year fixed effects. Standard errors were clustered at the hospital level. The figure includes incidence rate ratio estimates and 95% confidence intervals from regressions. For children's hospitals and CAHs, the reference group is other acute care hospitals. For hospital ownership type, the reference group is other nonprofit hospitals. For the two hospital size variables, the reference group is 100–299 staffed beds.

【FIGURE 3 · hesr70178-fig-0003】FIGURE 3 Coefficient plots for adult population. CAH, critical access hospital; ED, emergency department; E/M, evaluation & management; MRI, magnetic resonance imaging.
